claim: Thermodynamic models based on equilibrium statistical mechanics have emerged as a widespread theoretical framework to achieve predictive understanding of transcriptional regulation.
source: Thermodynamic models based on equilibrium statistical mechanics have emerged as a widespread theoretical framework to achieve this goal (Ackers et al., 1982; Vilar and Leibler, 2003; Bolouri and Davidson, 2003; Bintu et al., 2005b; Bintu et al., 2005a; Segal et al., 2008; Fakhouri et al., 2010; Sayal et al., 2016; Phillips et al., 2019; Eck et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work establishing thermodynamic models as a framework for transcriptional regulation.

claim: Over the last decade, thermodynamic models demonstrated the capacity to quantitatively predict bacterial transcriptional regulation from knowledge of the DNA regulatory architecture.
source: For instance, over the last decade, a dialogue between these thermodynamic models and experiments demonstrated the capacity to quantitatively predict bacterial transcriptional regulation from knowledge of the DNA regulatory architecture (He et al., 2010; Garcia and Phillips, 2011; Brewster et al., 2014; Garcia et al., 2012; Sepúlveda et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies demonstrating predictive capacity in bacterial systems.

claim: The hunchback P2 enhancer with six Bicoid binding sites exhibits strong Bicoid-Bicoid cooperativity such that the enhancer can either be unoccupied or completely bound by Bicoid molecules.
source: Here, we assume that Bicoid-Bicoid cooperativity is so strong that the enhancer can either be unoccupied or completely bound by Bicoid molecules (Gregor et al., 2007; Park et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and is used as an assumption in the model.

claim: Bicoid nuclear concentration dynamics were measured along the anterior-posterior axis of the embryo over nuclear cycles 13 and 14 using an eGFP-Bicoid line.
source: In order to quantify the concentration profile of Bicoid, we used an established eGFP-Bicoid line (Gregor et al., 2007) and measured mean Bicoid nuclear concentration dynamics along the anterior-posterior axis of the embryo over nuclear cycles 13 and 14 (nc13 and nc14, respectively) as shown in Movie Figure 3—video 1 (Eck et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental method described and citations to the eGFP-Bicoid line and measurement protocol.

claim: A new fly line harboring a fusion of a LlamaTag against eGFP to the endogenous runt gene was generated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homology-directed repair.
source: We therefore measured Runt concentration dynamics using our recently developed LlamaTags, which are devoid of such maturation dynamics artifacts (Bothma et al., 2018). Specifically, we generated a new fly line harboring a fusion of a LlamaTag against eGFP to the endogenous runt gene using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homology-directed repair (Materials and Methods; Harrison et al., 2010, Gratz et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the experimental method and citations to the LlamaTag technology and CRISPR methodology.

claim: There is a sex dependence in Runt nuclear concentration levels in nuclear cycle 13, with males displaying lower Runt levels than females.
source: As expected due to the location of the runt gene on the X chromosome (Lott et al., 2011), there is a sex dependence in the nuclear concentration levels in nc13, with males displaying lower Runt levels than females; this difference is compensated by early nc14 (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D, and is explained by the X chromosome location of the runt gene.

claim: The concentration dynamics of input transcription factors does not significantly affect the initial rate of RNAP loading.
source: To make this possible, we invoked previous observations stating that the concentration dynamics of input transcription factors does not significantly affect the initial rate of RNAP loading (Garcia et al., 2013; Eck et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The MS2 system enables fluorescent labeling of sites of active transcription in living embryos, with fluorescence intensity proportional to the number of actively transcribing RNAP molecules.
source: Here, we inserted 24 repeats of the MS2 loop sequence following the hunchback P2 enhancer and even-skipped promoter in our reporter construct, which leads to the fluorescent labeling of sites of active transcription in living embryos (Figure 3G and H; Movie Figure 3—video 3). The fluorescence intensity of each MS2 spot is proportional to the number of actively transcribing RNAP molecules (Garcia et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the MS2 system, reference to Figure 3G and H, and citation to Garcia et al., 2013.

claim: Unrepressed transcription rates varied significantly across synthetic enhancer constructs in the absence of Runt protein.
source: Notably, unrepressed transcription rates varied significantly across synthetic enhancers (Figure 4A). For example, despite no Runt being present, the [001] construct had almost twice the unrepressed rate of [000].
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The variability in unrepressed transcription rates stems from differences in RNAP-promoter interactions rather than differences in Bicoid binding or activation.
source: This suggests that the variability in unrepressed transcription rates due to the presence of Runt binding sites stems from differences in the behavior of RNAP at the promoter rather than differences in Bicoid binding or activation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the coefficient of variation analysis showing that RNAP-dependent parameters vary more than Bicoid-dependent parameters.

claim: A model where two Runt molecules bind and interact with RNAP independently from each other cannot predict repression by two Runt binding sites.
source: While there was some agreement between the model and the data for the [101] construct (Figure 6B, center), significant deviations from the prediction occurred for the other two constructs. These deviations ranged from less repression than predicted for [011] (Figure 6B, left) to more repression than predicted for [110] (Figure 6B, right). Thus, this simple model of Runt independent repression is not supported by the experimental data, suggesting additional regulatory interactions between the Runt molecules and RNAP.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of model predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Both Runt-Runt cooperativity and Runt-Runt-RNAP higher-order cooperativity are necessary to quantitatively describe repression by two Runt repressors.
source: Thus, while higher-order cooperativity is the main interaction necessary to quantitatively describe repression by two Runt repressors, pairwise cooperativity also needs to be invoked.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of different models with experimental data, showing that both types of cooperativity are needed.

claim: A parameter-free prediction using inferred parameters from one- and two-Runt binding sites constructs could not recapitulate the experimental data for three-Runt binding sites.
source: Figure 7A shows the resulting parameter-free prediction. As seen in the figure, our model could not qualitatively recapitulate the experimental data as it predicted too much repression.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of model predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Incorporating a Runt-Runt-Runt-RNAP higher-order cooperativity parameter enables the model to recapitulate the experimental data for three-Runt binding sites.
source: By including only a Runt-Runt-Runt-RNAP higher-order cooperativity parameter, our model recapitulated the experimental data (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MCMC fits to experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Higher-order cooperativity is necessary to account for regulation by two or more Runt repressor molecules.
source: We found that a thermodynamic model can recapitulate all our data. However, we also discovered that, while the model could describe repression by a single Runt repressor, protein-protein and higher-order cooperativities had to be invoked in order to quantitatively account for regulation by two or more repressor molecules.
evidence: The claim is supported by the results from modeling one-, two-, and three-Runt binding site constructs.

claim: The early embryo of Drosophila melanogaster has become one of the main workhorses for achieving a predictive understanding of cellular decision-making in development.
source: The early embryo of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has become one of the main workhorses in this attempt to achieve a predictive understanding of cellular decision-making in development due to its well-characterized gene regulatory network and transcription factor binding motifs, and the ease with which its development can be quantified using live imaging (Garcia et al., 2020; Small and Arnosti, 2020; Rivera et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies establishing Drosophila as a model system.

claim: The need to invoke higher-order cooperativity in eukaryotes only became apparent in the last few years.
source: The need to invoke this higher-order cooperativity in eukaryotes only became apparent in the last few years (Estrada et al., 2016b; Park et al., 2019; Biddle et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Higher-order cooperativity had been demonstrated in archaea and bacteria before being shown in eukaryotes.
source: The need to invoke this higher-order cooperativity in eukaryotes only became apparent in the last few years (Estrada et al., 2016b; Park et al., 2019; Biddle et al., 2020). These higher-order cooperativities might be necessary in order to account for the complex interactions mediated by, for example, the recruitment of co-repressors (Courey and Jia, 2001; Walrad et al., 2011), mediator complex (Park et al., 2019), or any other element of the transcriptional machinery.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the statement that higher-order cooperativity in eukaryotes only became apparent recently, combined with earlier citations to archaea and bacteria studies.

claim: The transcription time window was not significantly regulated in the presence of Runt.
source: Although these two quantities have been shown to be relevant in shaping gene expression patterns in other regulatory contexts (Garcia et al., 2013; Lammers et al., 2020; Eck et al., 2020; Dufourt et al., 2018; Reimer et al., 2021), we found that the transcription time window was not significantly regulated in the presence of Runt (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The LlamaTag-Runt allele rescues development to adulthood as a homozygous.
source: Importantly, this llamaTag-runt allele rescues development to adulthood as a homozygous. Thus we concluded that the LlamaTag-Runt allele can be used to monitor the behavior of endogenous Runt protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation of fly development.

claim: The initial rate of RNAP loading and accumulated mRNA levels show a strong correlation with a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.90.
source: Reassuringly, as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 8, our analysis revealed a strong correlation (with Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.90), supporting our claim that higher-order cooperativity is essential for explaining the action of multiple transcription factors during the development.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 8.

claim: The Bicoid-dependent parameters remain constant while RNAP-dependent parameters vary across synthetic enhancer constructs.
source: Using the thermodynamic model shown in Equation 3, we determined that the Bicoid-dependent parameters remain constant while RNAP-dependent parameters vary across these synthetic enhancer constructs.
evidence: The claim is supported by MCMC inference results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The overall enhancer sequence might affect the binding of the transcriptional machinery.
source: We speculate that the overall enhancer sequence, which changed as a result of the placement of different combinations of Runt binding sites within it, might affect the binding of the transcriptional machinery.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from the observed variability in RNAP-dependent parameters.

claim: The interaction energies for Runt-related cooperativity parameters are of a magnitude comparable to protein-protein interaction energies previously measured in bacterial systems.
source: An examination of the various cooperativity values inferred in the language of interaction energies (Table 1) revealed that these energies were of a magnitude comparable to protein-protein interaction energies previously measured in bacterial systems (Dodd et al., 2004; Bintu et al., 2005a; Amit et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of inferred interaction energies in Table 1 with cited bacterial studies.

claim: The [101] construct showed closer agreement with the parameter-free prediction without invoking higher-order cooperativity than the other two-Runt constructs.
source: Additionally, the [101] construct showed a closer agreement with the parameter-free prediction, without invoking higher-order cooperativity, than the other two constructs ([110] or [011]).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of model predictions with experimental data in Figure 6B.

claim: Higher-order cooperativity is sensitive to the placement and orientation of transcription factor binding sites within regulatory regions.
source: This further supports a picture where higher-order cooperativity is sensitive to the placement and orientation of transcription factor binding sites within regulatory regions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that different constructs require different cooperativity parameters.

claim: Synthetic minimal enhancers have emerged as an attractive alternative to endogenous enhancers for testing thermodynamic models.
source: To close this gap, synthetic minimal enhancers have emerged as an attractive alternative to endogenous enhancers (Fakhouri et al., 2010; Sayal et al., 2016; Park et al., 2019; Crocker et al., 2016). Here, the presence of only a handful of transcription factor binding sites and the ability to systematically control their placement and affinity dramatically reduce the number of free parameters in the model (Garcia et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies using synthetic enhancers.

claim: The hunchback P2 minimal enhancer provided an ideal scaffold for quantitatively and systematically dissecting repression by Runt.
source: Thus, hunchback P2 provided an ideal scaffold for quantitatively and systematically dissecting repression by Runt.
evidence: The claim is based on the properties of the hunchback P2 enhancer described in the preceding text.

claim: The MS2-MCP technique can be used to quantify patterns of accumulated mRNA, leading to results comparable to those obtained by smFISH.
source: Previous studies have shown that the MS2-MCP technique can also be used to quantify such patterns of accumulated mRNA, and that this quantification leads to results comparable to those obtained by smFISH (Garcia et al., 2013; Lammers et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The work establishes a framework for systematically and quantitatively studying repression in the early fly embryo.
source: Overall, the work presented here establishes a framework for systematically and quantitatively studying repression in the early fly embryo.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement of the study's contribution.

claim: Synthetic enhancers based on the hunchback P2 minimal enhancer constitute an ideal scaffold for the study of other repressors in early fly embryos.
source: As showcased here, synthetic enhancers based on the hunchback P2 minimal enhancer constitute an ideal scaffold for the study of other repressors in early fly embryos.
evidence: The claim is based on the success of the approach demonstrated in this study.
